questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Did the employee make the compensation claim pending (German: "Klage anhängig gemacht") within 180 days of the end of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the notice in writing?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Did the employee and the employer agree, after the notice, that the employment relationship would continue?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Did the employee lodge a written objection to the notice with the employer (German: "beim Kündigenden schriftlich Einsprache erheben") no later than the end of the notice period?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Was the employee, when notice was given, an elected employee representative on the staff council of the business or on a body linked to the business?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Have more than 180 days passed since the employment relationship ended?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Has the notice period (from the notice to the end of the employment relationship) already ended?

questions.label: Q9
questions.question: Was the notice given because the employee had asserted, in good faith, claims arising from the employment relationship?

text:
Hello,

Let me say first what this is not about. I never made any demands on Kirschbaum Holdings Ltd, no overtime, no pay rise, no complaints, nothing. So they can't claim I was a troublemaker, and I can't claim they punished me for asking for something.

The part I'm unsure about is my objection. On 24 July I wrote a short letter saying that I don't accept being let go, signed it and dropped it into the company letterbox in Schwyz myself. I didn't send it by registered post. Laura Carter, the managing director, now says nothing ever arrived. My colleague Rachel Lüthi thinks she saw it on the front desk, but she can't swear to it. So whether my objection ever reached them is still up in the air.

I should also say I was never on the staff committee or any kind of workers' council there. I was just one of the people in the warehouse.

The notice itself came on 18 June 2026. Ms Carter called me in and gave me a letter ending my job, without much explanation.

My employment ended on 31 July 2026, so that's less than two weeks ago.

I haven't gone to court or filed any claim for compensation anywhere yet, which is why I'm writing to you now. I'd like to know if it's worth it.

The notice period is over, I've had my last day and handed back my keys. I earned CHF 2,640 a month and I'm now looking for work.

What would you advise?

Regards,
Jack Baumann
Ahornweg 21, Schwyz
